purpose: Qualify one pre-CRC observable feature as a fair channel-gate ingredient for the strong combined baseline; compare the historical block-normalized AWGN workload with a fixed pre-fading noise power workload.
scope: Offline same-request paired conventional and NeuralRx correctness. This is neither a joint-policy superiority test nor a same-GPU MPS deadline test.

radio.receiver_order: conventional followed by NeuralRx on the identical immutable noisy slot

feature.online_candidate: mean squared magnitude of current-slot noisy PHY channel estimate

analysis.target: conventional branch correct TB, on the same request
analysis.gate_rule: skip NeuralRx and execute conventional only when observed channel-estimate power >= threshold
analysis.threshold_selection: On pre-fading train seed only, maximize skipped NeuralRx requests while losing at most 2/500 neural-only successes; break ties toward the higher threshold.
analysis.heldout_test: Apply the frozen threshold to the independent pre-fading test seed without retuning.
diagnostic_gates: At least 50/500 NeuralRx requests skipped on test
At most 5/500 neural-only successes lost on test
At least 50 neural-only successes available on test
Maximum measured feature GPU duration below 5 ms across all four arms
analysis.failure_disposition: If any diagnostic gate fails, do not represent this single-feature threshold as a qualified channel gate. Do not add seeds or change SNR to turn this protocol into PASS. A different observable feature requires a new calibration hypothesis and independent test trace.

limits: No training on held-out outcomes; no online admission is implemented here. Even PASS would establish only a baseline feature candidate in this synthetic channel model. It would not prove AI throughput gain, MPS isolation, production HARQ timing, or joint-policy novelty.
